title: keyword_matches word boundary check breaks on multi-byte UTF-8
description: posting.rs:210-221. The keyword_matches function uses byte-level indexing (content_bytes[abs_pos - 1].is_ascii_alphanumeric()) for word boundary detection. The .find() on line 215 operates on the lowercased string, and abs_pos is a byte offset. When abs_pos - 1 falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, content_bytes[abs_pos - 1] reads a continuation byte (0x80-0xBF), which is never ASCII alphanumeric. This means word boundaries around non-ASCII characters (accented letters, CJK) will always be treated as word boundaries. For CJK text this is arguably correct; for accented Latin text (e.g. 'café') it means a keyword at a byte boundary inside an accented character might match incorrectly as a 'whole word'.
